CONTEXT: We operate an LLM-agent-run product-development system re-founding its quality layer on construction-definitions-precede-checks. An existing research report at /workspace/drafts/definition-format-research.md surveys established definition formats (process/role/artifact/principle/quality/fitness-test/context-governance) and recommends adopt/adapt/bespoke per element. A completeness critique found missing traditions. Your findings will be integrated into that report. EVIDENCE BAR: primary sources; never cite a source you have not confirmed exists; separate describing from recommending. Web access: if WebSearch/WebFetch are unavailable, load via ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch".

TASK: Survey the quality-management lineage missing from the report. Cover: ISO 9001:2015 documented-information requirements and document-control practice (clause 7.5 — creation/update/control, the controlled-document concept, versioning and audit traceability) and ISO 9000:2015 vocabulary; the Shewhart/Deming PDCA cycle as an improvement-loop FORM (original sources: Shewhart 1939, Deming's PDSA lectures; where each phase's expected outputs live); Six Sigma CTQ (critical-to-quality) trees — the canonical derivation from qualitative customer need to measurable characteristic to specification/check, with a primary or authoritative secondary source; DMAIC as a defined process-with-phase-gates form. For each: exact form elements, citation, and fit for a system deriving mechanical checks and rubrics from ratified construction definitions and governing versioned prompt/skill/definition surfaces.

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- bring-up-bc: Launch an already-scaffolded Bounded Context as a running, online container and verify it reaches the online state
- company-research: Build a cited, bounded intelligence brief on a competitor, peer product, or alternative framework — strategy, product philosophy, recent moves — to ground a brief/PDR in external reality instead of intuition. Use for the consumer-product competitive/market input to problem discovery, or to study a competing framework.
- create-bc: Create a new Bounded Context from scratch — scaffold, remote, manifest registration, and brokered launch — as the lead shop
- derisk-measurement-advisor: Scan a shaping candidate for risk across 10 dimensions — 4 internal (Desirability, Usability, Feasibility, Viability) and 6 external (PESTEL) — and triage each into act-now or track, so the candidate's rabbit-holes and risks name what to test before committing. Reach for it when a bet feels roadmap-ready and you want a structured "what could go wrong, internally and externally?"
- discovery-dialogue: Run the open, interactive discovery conversation that turns a directional or ambiguous prompt into a written, grounded intent record
- discovery-interview-prep: Design a customer discovery interview plan — research goal, target segment, access constraints, and a bias-resistant question set — so a discovery-dialogue turn produces real learning instead of confirmation. Use when the intent record rests on an assumed job that needs to be heard from a real user.
- discovery-process: The end-to-end discovery arc — frame, plan, research, synthesize, validate, decide — used to sequence a multi-turn discovery-dialogue and know which technique skill comes next. Use when a discovery is large enough to need staging rather than a single lens.
- eol-message: Empathetic end-of-life announcement for a retiring product or capability — acknowledges disruption, explains the change as progress, and gives a concrete migration path. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session, and specifically when a brief flips to status:retired.
- incoming-request-advisor: Decode an incoming request before responding — separate the literal ask from the job-behind-it, read the sender's power and stake, and surface hidden assumptions — so a request is classified by its real outcome, not its surface wording. Use at PM-mode entry, at the router's classification boundary, to decide whether a request needs a discovery-dialogue at all.
- jobs-to-be-done: Uncover the stable job a user is hiring the product to do — functional, social, emotional — plus their pains and gains, so intent anchors on a validated job instead of a feature request. Use during the discovery-dialogue when a request smells solution-shaped ("add X").
- opportunity-solution-tree: Move from a target outcome down through opportunities (problems) to candidate solutions to a chosen bet, so shaping commits the candidate to the right problem before it converges on a sketch. Reach for it when a request arrives outcome-shaped or solution-shaped and you need to keep "what are we moving?" upstream of "what do we build?"
- option-tradeoff: Frame two or more shaped options against each other, surface the tradeoffs, and run the deciding conversation with the product authority
- pol-probe: Design a Proof-of-Life probe — a lightweight, disposable experiment that tests one falsifiable hypothesis before expensive work — and land it in the candidate's evidence/experiments line. Reach for it when a shape rests on an assumption cheap enough to test in hours or days and honest enough to kill the bet if it fails.
- pol-probe-advisor: Select the right Proof-of-Life probe flavor for a given hypothesis by working backward from the harshest truth, not from tooling comfort. Reach for it inside shaping when you know an assumption needs testing but aren't sure whether it's a feasibility check, a task test, a narrative, a simulation, or a vibe-coded probe.
- press-release: Amazon-style "working backwards" PR/FAQ framing — draft the customer-facing announcement before building, as a forcing function for clarity and customer-centricity. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session to test whether a direction is genuinely compelling from the outside.
- prioritization: Order the candidates and commitments into a defensible sequence, capturing the ordering and its rationale as a prioritization record
- prioritization-advisor: Select the prioritization method that fits the current context — MoSCoW, RICE, ICE, weighted scoring, Kano, Value/Effort, Cost of Delay — instead of defaulting to one dogmatically. Reach for it inside a prioritization session before scoring anything, to pick the right lens for the stage, data, and decision at hand.
- problem-framing-canvas: Reframe a messy or solution-shaped request into a clear, bias-checked problem statement and a "How Might We" question before committing intent. Use inside the discovery-dialogue when you suspect you're about to solve the wrong problem.
- problem-space-mapping: Continuously maintain the map of the product's problem space so every candidate and intent has a place to hang, producing problem-space map revisions
- problem-statement: Turn a request or a raw job into a crisp, user-centered problem statement using the "I am / trying to / but / because / which makes me feel" frame, so intent names a person and a barrier, not a solution. Use inside the discovery-dialogue to fix the problem before any solutioning.
- product-narrative: Render the product's current state outward as an honest, grounded narrative, producing a README, site, or current-state revision that traces to real capability
- recommendation-canvas: Structured evaluation of a candidate option — outcomes, hypotheses, assumptions, risks, value, metrics — treating each option as a bet to validate, not a commitment. Reach for it inside an option-tradeoff session to turn a raw option list into a defensible pick with rationale.
- reconcile-and-close: Reconcile a completed BC dispatch by consuming its work_done outbox row and closing the corresponding bead as one atomic reconcile-and-close action via the reconcile-and-close executable wrapper
- shaping: Take a validated intent and drive a single candidate to shaped — bounded, de-risked, and ready for a commitment decision
- stakeholder-engagement-advisor: Plan engagement for one specific stakeholder — diagnose their profile and power/impact position, then tailor message, medium, cadence, and a named next action, planning both sides of the relationship. Use inside the discovery-dialogue when the intent hinges on a critical or resistant stakeholder whose input you must actually secure.
- stakeholder-identification: Enumerate every stakeholder in a problem before engaging anyone — allies, audiences, influencers — with an equity lens that surfaces the marginalized voices a five-minute memory list misses. Use inside the discovery-dialogue to be sure the intent isn't framed for only the loudest party.
- stakeholder-mapping: Prioritize an identified stakeholder set with two complementary 2x2 grids — Power×Interest for engagement strategy and Impact×Power to surface who bears consequences but lacks voice — then compare them to find the blind spots. Use inside the discovery-dialogue after identification to decide whose voice the intent must elevate.
- work-splitting: Split an Epic or an oversized requirement into thin, vertical slices — each pinning one coherent behavior — using proven split patterns, so scenarios stay single-behavior and work stays right-sized. Use when decomposing an Epic into scenarios, when a scenario carries multiple When/Then, or when an assigned unit is too big to build and review cleanly.
- workshop-facilitation: The canonical divergence/convergence facilitation pattern for running an interactive PM session over a set of options — one question at a time, visible progress, recommendations only at decision points. Reach for it inside an option-tradeoff session to structure how the dialogue is conducted.
- write-adr: Use when the author is authoring or creating a adr artifact — a generated guide that drives the adr to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the adr kind.
- write-brief: Use when the author is authoring or creating a brief artifact — a generated guide that drives the brief to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the brief kind.
- write-candidate: Use when the author is authoring or creating a candidate artifact — a generated guide that drives the candidate to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the candidate kind.
- write-current-state: Use when the author is authoring or creating a current-state artifact — a generated guide that drives the current-state to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the current-state kind.
- write-intent-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a intent-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the intent-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the intent-record kind.
- write-pdr: Use when the author is authoring or creating a pdr artifact — a generated guide that drives the pdr to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the pdr kind.
- write-prioritization-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a prioritization-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the prioritization-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the prioritization-record kind.
- write-session-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a session-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the session-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the session-record kind.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Definition-format research: established forms for the quality-layer seed
2	
3	**Status: SITTING MATERIAL — not ratified, decides nothing.** This document
4	describes established external forms and recommends candidates; every decision
5	in it belongs to the product authority. Date: 2026-08-05. Produced by the
6	definition-format research directed in the re-founding dialogue (the
7	construction-definitions-precede-checks re-founding of the quality layer).
8	
9	Conventions: every claim carries a citation to a verified source. Where the
10	research corpus contained a described inaccuracy, the corrected fact is used
11	here and marked "(corrected)".
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Survey
16	
17	This section DESCRIBES what exists. It recommends nothing; recommendations are
18	confined to section 2.
19	
20	### 1.1 Process definition formats
21	
22	The ISO/IEC JTC1/SC7 line contains a purpose-built specification for process
23	description: ISO/IEC/IEEE 24774:2021 (Systems and software engineering — Life
24	cycle management — Specification for process description, 1st ed., May 2021,
25	superseding ISO/IEC TR 24774:2010; iso.org/standard/78981.html). Its clause 5.3
26	required elements are exactly three: process name, purpose, and outcomes; its
27	clause 5.4 optional elements are activities, tasks, notes, inputs, outputs, and
28	controls and constraints. Outcomes are short declarative, observable,
29	assessable results. The process name is a descriptive noun phrase — the
30	standard warns against verb-noun phrasing, which belongs to activities and
31	tasks (corrected: an earlier research pass mis-stated this as a verb phrase).
32	Clause 6 defines process views/viewpoints; clause 7 defines conformance claims.
33	The standard prescribes description, not execution: it carries no workflow or
34	sequencing semantics.
35	
36	ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 (System life cycle processes) and ISO/IEC/IEEE
37	12207:2017 (Software life cycle processes) are the large worked corpus written
38	in that convention: roughly 30 processes each, every one rendered as title,
39	one-sentence purpose, 3–8 declarative outcomes, then activities decomposed into
40	shall-level tasks, grouped into agreement / organizational project-enabling /
41	technical management / technical categories (standards.ieee.org/ieee/15288/10424/).
42	
43	The ISO/IEC 330xx process-assessment family (ISO/IEC 33001:2015, 33004:2015,
44	measurement framework in 33020; superseding ISO/IEC 15504 as of March 2015;
45	iso.org/standard/54175.html) formalizes the connection between definitions and
46	checks: a Process Reference Model describes each process by purpose + outcomes
47	only and must be free of capability/measurement aspects; a Process Assessment
48	Model then maps assessment indicators — base practices and work products — onto
49	those outcomes; a measurement framework adds rated process attributes. Checks
50	are formally derived from, and traceable to, purpose+outcome definitions.
51	
52	ETVX (Radice, Roth, O'Hara, Ciarfella, "A Programming Process Architecture",
53	IBM Systems Journal 24(2), 1985, pp. 79–90) is the lightest classic
54	per-activity frame: Entry criteria, Task set, Validation conditions, eXit
55	criteria per activity cell, composable by chaining, with no ordering engine.
56	(Corrected: the original expansion is Validation, not Verification; both
57	renderings circulate in CMM-lineage secondary literature. A free scan exists at
58	bitsavers.org despite the IBM Systems Journal paywall.) It is the only classic
59	form that builds verification into the definition cell itself.
60	
61	OMG Essence 1.2 (SEMAT; OMG formal/18-10-02, 2018; Essence 2.0 in beta with
62	formal publication scheduled March 2026; omg.org/spec/Essence/1.2) defines
63	progress and health rather than workflow: Alphas (essential trackable concerns)
64	with ordered named states, each state carrying a short qualitative checklist;
65	activities whose completion criteria are expressed in terms of alpha states and
66	work-product levels of detail — a definition-level termination semantic
67	requiring no engine; competencies with five levels; practice/method
68	composition; a card presentation format.
69	
70	CMMI contributes a structural trichotomy: in CMMI for Development V1.3
71	(CMU/SEI-2010-TR-033, 2010) goals are required components, practices are
72	expected, and subpractices/example work products are informative — appraisal
73	targets goal achievement, not practice performance; CMMI V3.0 (ISACA, 2023)
74	recasts this as practice areas with intent and value statements and
75	evolutionary practice-group levels. ITIL v3 (Service Design, 2011 ed., Cabinet
76	Office/TSO) documents every process in one fixed section skeleton (purpose/
77	objectives, scope, value, policies, activities, triggers/inputs/outputs/
78	interfaces, CSFs with nested KPIs, risks), and ITIL 4 (AXELOS, 2019; 34
79	practice guides) does the same for practices — success factors and metrics
80	nested under the definition.
81	
82	Notation standards exist but describe flow or I/O, not construction quality:
83	BPMN 2.0 (OMG formal/2011-01-03; ISO/IEC 19510:2013, which is technically BPMN
84	2.0.1) with its Descriptive vs Analytic vs Common Executable conformance
85	sub-classes; CMMN 1.0/1.1 (OMG, 2014; Marin, arXiv:1608.05011) — declarative
86	case plans with sentries (entry/exit criteria), milestones, and discretionary
87	items, the standards world's clearest vocabulary for unpredictable
88	knowledge-work; IDEF0 (NIST FIPS PUB 183, 1993, withdrawn as a federal
89	standard in 2008; IEEE 1320.1-1998; ISO/IEC/IEEE 31320-1:2012) with its
90	Input/Control/Output/Mechanism arrow typing; and PMBOK 6th ed. ITTOs (PMI,
91	2017), which the PMBOK 7th ed. (2021) itself dropped from the core. ISO/IEC
92	24744:2014 (SEMDM) models method-level and endeavor-level views of one concept
93	via powertypes; its uptake is essentially academic.
94	
95	### 1.2 Role definition formats
96	
97	OMG SPEM 2.0 (formal/2008-04-01, April 2008; omg.org/spec/SPEM/2.0) draws a
98	hard structural line between Method Content — reusable Role Definitions
99	(skills, responsibilities), Task Definitions, Work Product Definitions, typed
100	Guidance including checklists — and Process, which arranges content occurrences
101	into lifecycles. A full knowledge base of role/task/artifact definitions can be
102	maintained without ever creating a process. Eclipse EPF Composer
103	(projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.epf; archived, last release 2018) is
104	the working proof: method plugins publish role/task/work-product/guidance pages
105	as a browsable static site, no engine. RUP (Kruchten, The Rational Unified
106	Process: An Introduction, 3rd ed., Addison-Wesley, 2003, ch. 3) is the
107	ancestor form: roles carry responsibilities plus required competencies, and
108	every artifact has exactly one responsible role.
109	
110	The Scrum Guide (Schwaber & Sutherland, November 2020, scrumguides.org) defines
111	roles as short accountability lists — 4–8 bullets of what the holder is
112	answerable for, not task scripts.
113	
114	In current agent practice, the Claude Code subagent definition
115	(code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) is a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter
116	is the delegation and capability contract (required name and description;
117	optional tools/disallowedTools, model, maxTurns, skills preload list, memory
118	scope) and whose body is the role's standing system prompt. The shop already
119	uses this container for lead-po and lead-architect.
120	
121	### 1.3 Artifact / document-type schema formats
122	
123	ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289:2019 (Content of life-cycle information items, 4th ed.;
124	earlier editions 2011/2015/2017; iso.org/standard/74909.html) is the
125	established meta-format: every information item is classified as one of seven
126	generic document types — description, plan, policy, procedure, report, request,
127	specification — each generic type carrying generic content requirements, and
128	each named item carrying specific required-content clauses. It is explicitly
129	medium-independent, and its mapping tables tie information items to the
130	12207/15288 processes that produce and consume them.
131	
132	RUP artifacts (Kruchten 2003, ch. 3) ship with templates and checkpoints —
133	per-artifact review checklists attached to the artifact definition. The 2020
134	Scrum Guide pairs every artifact with exactly one commitment (Product Backlog →
135	Product Goal, Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal, Increment → Definition of Done);
136	the DoD is "a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets
137	the quality measures required for the product," with a defined consequence:
138	non-conforming work returns to the Product Backlog. Microsoft Prompty
139	(prompty.ai/core-concepts/file-format; microsoft/prompty) demonstrates a
140	schema-validated asset format whose frontmatter declares inputs, outputs, and
141	per-input sample/default data. The MCP resources primitive (Model Context
142	Protocol spec 2025-06-18) standardizes inclusion-decision metadata on context
143	artifacts: audience, priority 0.0–1.0, lastModified.
144	
145	### 1.4 Principle statement formats
146	
147	TOGAF (The Open Group, TOGAF 9.2, "Architecture Principles" chapter, carried
148	into the 10th Edition ADM Techniques volume; pubs.opengroup.org) is the only
149	broadly adopted formal template specifically for principles: Name / Statement
150	(one-sentence unambiguous rule) / Rationale (business-language why) /
151	Implications (required actions and impacts), plus five quality criteria for
152	the set — Understandable, Robust (enables good decisions and enforceable
153	policies), Complete, Consistent, Stable (enduring but amendable under a change
154	process). The standard thus already pairs a construction definition with
155	derived quality criteria.
156	
157	Sentence-level normative language has two established conventions. IETF BCP 14
158	(RFC 2119, Bradner 1997; RFC 8174, Leiba 2017; datatracker.ietf.org) defines
159	MUST/SHOULD/MAY keyword families, restricts normative force to ALL-CAPS
160	(8174), requires an opt-in boilerplate, and rules that imperatives be used
161	sparingly and never to mandate implementation method. ISO/IEC Directives Part 2
162	(9th ed., 2021) binds one modal verb per provision type (shall=requirement,
163	should=recommendation, may=permission, can=possibility; "must" reserved for
164	external constraints), requires that requirements be objectively verifiable or
165	not stated as requirements, bans subjective qualifiers, and mandates an
166	explicit normative/informative split.
167	
168	Decision records are a distinct, established artifact kind: the Nygard ADR
169	(cognitect.com blog, 15 Nov 2011) — Title/Context/Decision/Status/Consequences,
170	value-neutral context, active-voice "We will…", consequences including
171	negatives, append-only numbering, supersede-never-rewrite, 1–2 pages; MADR
172	v4.0.0 (adr.github.io/madr, September 2024) — Markdown Architectural Decision
173	Records (corrected: v4.0.0 reverted the v3-era "Any Decision Records"
174	expansion) — adds Considered Options, Decision Drivers, an optional
175	Confirmation section stating how compliance will be verified, and YAML front
176	matter; and Y-statements (Zdun, Capilla, Tran, Zimmermann, "Sustainable
177	Architectural Design Decisions", IEEE Software 30(6), 2013,
178	doi:10.1109/MS.2013.97) — a one-sentence template whose clauses name the
179	rejected alternatives (canonically "neglected") and the accepted downside.
180	
181	Principle fitness criteria exist in the literature: Rumelt (Good Strategy Bad
182	Strategy, Crown Business, 2011) — a guiding policy "directs and constrains
183	action without fully defining it"; bad-strategy hallmarks fluff and
184	goals-mistaken-for-strategy; Spool ("Creating Great Design Principles: 6
185	Counter-intuitive Tests", UIE, March 2011; articles.centercentre.com) —
186	evidence-derived, helps-you-say-no, distinguishes-from-competitors,
187	reversible-in-context, per-project revalidated, meaning-calibrated-on-real-work;
188	Lencioni ("Make Your Values Mean Something", HBR 80(7), July 2002) — core vs
189	aspirational vs permission-to-play vs accidental values. Trade-off grammars:
190	the Agile Manifesto value pairs with the right-side-still-has-value qualifier
191	(agilemanifesto.org, 2001) and even/over statements — good-vs-good pairs with
192	declared priority (Dignan, Brave New Work, Portfolio/Penguin, 2019; Kamer,
193	"Even/Over Statements", The Ready on Medium, 2021). Operated exemplars: the
194	W3C TAG Web Platform Design Principles (w3ctag.github.io/design-principles;
195	living note, updated June 2026) — imperative titles with parenthetical stable
196	names, prose, worked examples, applied in actual spec reviews — and the GOV.UK
197	Government Design Principles (gov.uk, 2012, updated April 2025; now 11
198	principles), an amend-in-place principle set with public revision history.
199	
200	### 1.5 Content-quality guideline and rubric formats
201	
202	Educational assessment supplies the descriptor-rubric family: Brookhart (How
203	to Create and Use Rubrics, ASCD, 2013) — criteria about the quality of the
204	work, crossed with 3–5 prose performance-level descriptors of observable
205	features (not evaluative adjectives); analytic (per-criterion judgment) vs
206	holistic (single judgment) variants. The AAC&U VALUE rubrics (aacu.org/value/
207	rubrics; 15 rubrics developed 2007–2009, a 16th added 2013 — corrected) are the
208	mature exemplar artifact: Definition + Framing Language + Glossary preamble,
209	then a criteria-by-levels matrix with named ordered levels Capstone /
210	Milestones / Benchmark, with an explicit localization instruction. The
211	single-point rubric (Fluckiger, Delta Kappa Gamma Bulletin 76(4), 2010)
212	authors only the proficient-standard column, with blank flanking columns for
213	observed shortfalls and excesses.
214	
215	Binary gates: the Scrum DoD (2020 Scrum Guide) — one uniform itemized quality
216	contract with a consequence rule; acceptance criteria in scenario-oriented
217	Given/When/Then form (Gherkin; cucumber.io/docs/gherkin; Adzic, Specification
218	by Example, Manning, 2011) or rule-oriented list form; and checklist design
219	constraints from Gawande (The Checklist Manifesto, Metropolitan Books, 2009)
220	and the Gawande/Boorman "Checklist for Checklists" (projectcheck.org):
221	DO-CONFIRM vs READ-DO typing, named pause points, 5–9 killer items, ~60–90
222	second budget, field validation. Fagan inspections (IBM Systems Journal 15(3),
223	1976; Brykczynski's checklist survey, ACM SIGSOFT SEN 24(1), 1999) derive and
224	continuously re-derive checklist items from observed defect data.
225	
226	Quality taxonomies: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 (SQuaRE product quality model) — nine
227	characteristics decomposed into defined sub-characteristics, deliberately a
228	vocabulary separated from measures (2502n) and requirements (25030).
229	
230	Style-guide governance: the Google developer documentation style guide
231	(developers.google.com/style, public since September 2017) and the Microsoft
232	Writing Style Guide (learn.microsoft.com/style-guide, 2018–present) converge on
233	one anatomy — voice principles, a condensed highlights/top-10 layer, topical
234	rule pages with before/after examples, an A–Z word list, and an explicit
235	precedence hierarchy (project sheet → this guide → named fallbacks). The Vale
236	prose linter (vale.sh; LWN, "Vale: enforcing style guidelines for text", 2024)
237	mechanizes such guides: each YAML rule carries a check pattern, a severity
238	tier, and a link back to the guideline it enforces, packaged per style guide
239	with per-project overrides — checks derived from definitions, running in the
240	wild.
241	
242	Two architectural devices recur: Deming's operational definition (Out of the
243	Crisis, MIT Press, 1986, ch. 9) — a quality adjective has "no communicable
244	meaning" until expressed as sampling/test procedure + criterion + yes/no
245	decision rule; and WCAG 2.2's conformance architecture (W3C Recommendation, 5
246	Oct 2023) — principles → guidelines → 86 individually testable success criteria
247	(A:31, AA:24, AAA:31; corrected — 4.1.1 Parsing was removed as obsolete, so the
248	commonly repeated 87/A:32 count is wrong), with a strict normative/informative
249	split: criteria bind, Understanding and Techniques documents inform. Google's
250	code-review guidance (google.github.io/eng-practices) is a two-layer review
251	rubric: one senior decision principle (approve once the change "definitely
252	improves the overall code health," even if imperfect) plus an enumerated aspect
253	list, with authority routing (style → style guide/linter; design → principles).
254	The Federal Plain Language Guidelines (PLAIN, 2011, pursuant to the Plain
255	Writing Act of 2010, Pub. L. 111-274; originally plainlanguage.gov/guidelines,
256	now hosted at digital.gov/guides/plain-language — corrected URL) contribute the
257	imperative one-behavior-per-rule granularity with before/after example pairs.
258	
259	### 1.6 Qualitative fitness-test formats for LLM output
260	
261	The research base: Zheng et al., "Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and
262	Chatbot Arena" (NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2306.05685) established LLM-judge viability
263	(>80% agreement with humans) and named position, verbosity, and
264	self-enhancement bias, with mitigations (position swap, reference-guided
265	grading, chain-of-thought). Zheng et al., "Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks"
266	(ICLR 2025 oral; arXiv:2410.07137) proved judges are adversarially gameable: a
267	constant null-model response reached 86.5% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0.
268	G-Eval (Liu et al., EMNLP 2023; arXiv:2303.16634) canonized the derivation
269	procedure criteria → evaluation steps → judged score (Spearman 0.514 on
270	summarization). EvalGen (Shankar et al., UIST 2024; arXiv:2404.12272)
271	established criteria drift: humans discover criteria by grading outputs, so
272	criteria sets cannot be fully specified a priori and need an iterative
273	human-calibration loop. CheckList (Ribeiro et al., ACL 2020 Best Paper;
274	arXiv:2005.04118) is the pre-LLM precedent for small targeted behavioral
275	probes (MFT/INV/DIR types over a capability matrix).
276	
277	Production tooling converges on scenario + plain-language criteria + LLM judge:
278	promptfoo (promptfoo.dev) — declarative YAML tests with vars and llm-rubric
279	assertions co-resident with deterministic checks, plus a scenarios construct;
280	DeepEval GEval (deepeval.com) — criteria/evaluation_steps in Python; Ragas
281	(docs.ragas.io) — score-anchored rubrics (a written description per score
282	level) and binary Aspect Critique; LangSmith/OpenEvals (docs.langchain.com;
283	langchain-ai/openevals) — judge factories with binary-preferred, exemplar-
284	anchored authoring guidance; Braintrust autoevals
285	(github.com/braintrustdata/autoevals) — constrained choice→score classification;
286	OpenAI evals (github.com/openai/evals; hosted platform deprecated: read-only
287	Oct 2026, shutdown Nov 2026) — the ancestral JSONL+YAML model-graded registry.
288	Anthropic's guidance ("Define success criteria / build evaluations", platform
289	docs; "Demystifying evals for AI agents", engineering blog, Jan 2026)
290	prescribes a grader hierarchy (code-based → LLM → human calibration), one
291	isolated judge per quality dimension, constrained outputs with anchored scales,
292	and frequent human calibration. LangWatch Scenario (github.com/langwatch/
293	scenario) is the closest living relative of the shop's proposal: named
294	scenarios with a situation description, a criteria list of plain-language
295	expectations, and a Judge Agent returning verdict + reasoning, CI-runnable.
296	
297	The BDD×LLM literature runs the opposite direction from the shop's proposal —
298	LLMs generating or assessing Gherkin (arXiv:2403.14965; arXiv:2508.20744;
299	arXiv:2607.01980; arXiv:2512.01232, "LLM-as-a-Judge for Scalable Test Coverage
300	Evaluation"). No established named standard exists for authoring Gherkin as
301	fitness specifications judged (not executed) by an LLM; the pattern exists only
302	as the near-neighbors above. See section 3.
303	
304	### 1.7 Compiled-context and skill governance
305	
306	Anthropic Agent Skills (platform.claude.com/docs — "Skill authoring best
307	practices"; anthropic.com/engineering — "Equipping agents for the real world",
308	Oct 2025): a skill is a directory with SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + body) under
309	three-tier progressive disclosure — name+description (max 64 chars / 1,024
310	chars, description stating both what and when) always in context; body (<500
311	lines) on trigger; references (one level deep) on demand. Authoring rules
312	include degrees-of-freedom calibration (high/medium/low), evaluation-first
313	development ("Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation") with
314	an eval structure of {skills, query, files, expected_behavior[]} and a
315	three-scenario minimum, and a pre-share checklist. Claude Code memory
316	(code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) layers managed-policy > user > project > local
317	CLAUDE.md files (broadest-first, nearest read last), @imports to depth four,
318	path-scoped .claude/rules with glob frontmatter, a <200-line budget, a content
319	discriminator (standing facts stay; multi-step or localized procedure moves to
320	a skill or path-scoped rule), a verifiable-specificity rule, and the boundary
321	that CLAUDE.md is context while hard constraints belong in hooks/settings. The
322	subagent format (section 1.2) supplies the role container.
323	
324	Adjacent conventions: AGENTS.md (agents.md) — a schema-less well-known file
325	with nested nearest-wins precedence; Cursor rules (cursor.com/docs/context/
326	rules) — .mdc files whose frontmatter field combinations encode four activation
327	modes (Always / Intelligently / Specific Files / Manual), <500-line budget,
328	org-level Team Rules precedence; llms.txt (Howard, Answer.AI, Sept 2024;
329	llmstxt.org) — a fixed-grammar curated index (H1, summary, annotated H2 link
330	lists, an explicit Optional degradation tier); MCP prompts and resources
331	(modelcontextprotocol.io, spec 2025-06-18) — the user-/application-/model-
332	controlled taxonomy and the audience/priority/lastModified annotation
333	vocabulary; Langfuse prompt version control (langfuse.com/docs) — immutable
334	version IDs plus mutable deployment labels, protected promotion, diffs;
335	promptfoo declarative eval configs (promptfoo.dev/docs/intro) — versioned
336	prompts × providers × tests with mixed deterministic and model-graded
337	assertions gating CI; Prompty (section 1.3) — a schema-validated asset with
338	declared I/O and sample data; and Anthropic's context-engineering principles
339	(anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents) — the
340	smallest high-signal token set, right-altitude prompts, named sections,
341	just-in-time retrieval, sub-agents returning condensed 1,000–2,000-token
342	summaries.
343	
344	---
345	
346	## 2. Recommendations
347	
348	Each recommendation names adopt / adapt (with deltas) / bespoke (with
349	justification), sketches the concrete in-system shape, and cites sources.
350	Nothing here is decided.
351	
352	**2.1 Process definitions — adopt ISO/IEC/IEEE 24774 header + ETVX activity
353	cells; adapt 330xx derivation and Essence/CMMN termination vocabulary.**
354	Each shop process definition: a noun-phrase name, one-sentence purpose, and
355	3–8 observable outcomes per 24774:2021 clause 5.3, phrased in the 15288/12207
356	outcome style ("An X is produced/defined"); each activity inside it an ETVX
357	cell — entry criteria (the trigger side of "resulting actions"), tasks,
358	validation conditions, exit criteria (Radice et al. 1985). Long-running loops
359	terminate by definition-level state, not step count: exit criteria expressed as
360	reached states with short checklists (Essence 1.2 alpha-state form; CMMN's
361	"milestone with entry criteria" and "exit criterion on a stage" as citable
362	vocabulary — vocabulary only, not the notation). Checks derive per the 330xx
363	pattern: outcomes → assessment indicators → rubric items, with traceability but
364	without capability levels, maturity staging, or assessor machinery (delta).
365	CMMI's required/expected/informative trichotomy separates what must be true
366	(checkable) from typical ways to do it (guidance) inside each definition.
367	BPMN/IDEF0/PMBOK ITTO are not adopted; a descriptive-class diagram may
368	occasionally illustrate a handoff, rendered in mermaid.
369	
370	**2.2 Role definitions — adopt the Claude Code subagent container; adapt Scrum
371	accountability lists and the SPEM content/process split as its discipline.**
372	Concretely: role = .claude/agents file where the frontmatter is the routing and
373	capability contract (description as delegation trigger; tools allowlist derived
374	from the role's do-not list; skills preload list as the declared role→activity
375	binding, making the compiled surface enumerable and diffable; maxTurns as a
376	standard termination bound) and the body is the standing identity written as a
377	Scrum-style accountability list (4–8 answerable-for bullets, 2020 Scrum Guide)
378	plus RUP-style required competencies (Kruchten 2003). The SPEM 2.0 separation
379	is the governing rule: roles and skills are Method Content; no ordering or
380	lifecycle text lives in a role definition. RUP's one-responsible-role-per-
381	artifact rule binds each artifact kind to exactly one accountable role.
382	
383	**2.3 Artifact/document-type schemas — adopt the 15289 two-level scheme; adapt
384	with Scrum commitments and Prompty-style validated frontmatter.**
385	Concretely: a small set of shop generic types (description, plan, record,
386	request, specification — pruned from 15289:2019's seven), each with generic
387	content requirements; each named kind (brief, PDR, ADR, session record…) with
388	specific required-content clauses, exactly the shape the existing write-*
389	kind-schema mechanism already has — 15289 is the external anchor, not a
390	migration. Deltas: (a) every artifact kind carries one commitment — a small
391	DoD-style qualitative criteria set with a stated consequence on failure (2020
392	Scrum Guide artifact-commitment pairing; RUP checkpoints as the derived review
393	checklist precedent); (b) frontmatter is schema-validated and declares expected
394	inputs/outputs plus at least one worked sample (Prompty), and carries
395	audience/priority/lastModified-style inclusion metadata (MCP resources
396	annotation vocabulary); (c) 15289-style mapping tables tie each process
397	definition's outcomes to the artifact kinds it produces.
398	
399	**2.4 Principles — adopt the TOGAF four-part template and BCP 14 keywords;
400	adapt ISO Directives rules; keep decisions in ADRs, separate.**
401	Concretely: each principle is Name / Statement / Rationale / Implications
402	(TOGAF), the Name rendered as an imperative title with a parenthetical stable
403	handle for citation in reviews (W3C TAG form); even/over grammar (Dignan 2019;
404	The Ready) is an approved Statement form for priority-call principles, with the
405	Agile Manifesto's right-side-still-has-value qualifier attached. All definition
406	kinds — not just principles — adopt BCP 14 (RFC 2119/8174) keyword discipline
407	with the boilerplate, which is directly lintable; from ISO/IEC Directives Part
408	2 adopt three rules only (delta: not the ISO document skeleton): one modal per
409	provision type, requirements must be verifiable or be demoted, explicit
410	normative/informative tagging. Decisions stay a distinct kind: the shop already
411	writes Nygard-form ADRs; MADR v4.0.0's Confirmation section and Decision
412	Drivers, and the Y-statement one-liner (Zdun et al. 2013) as a required summary
413	field, are the named deltas worth folding in. Principles are standing and
414	amended under change control (TOGAF Stable); ADRs are immutable and superseded
415	(Nygard). The principle fitness-test set is assembled — not invented — from
416	TOGAF's five criteria, Spool's tests 2/3/4, Rumelt's fluff and goal-vs-policy
417	anti-patterns, and Lencioni's permission-to-play/aspirational screen; this
418	composition is the only quasi-bespoke element, justified as assembly of
419	published criteria.
420	
421	**2.5 Content-quality guidelines and rubrics — adopt Deming's meta-rule,
422	single-point rubrics, DoD gates, Gawande constraints, the Google two-layer
423	review form, and the style-guide + Vale enforcement anatomy.**
424	Concretely: (a) Deming's three elements (test procedure, criterion, yes/no
425	decision — Out of the Crisis ch. 9) are the acceptance test applied to every
426	definition the seed layer produces; an unoperationalized adjective is not yet a
427	check. (b) Per-artifact-kind fitness sets take single-point rubric form
428	(Fluckiger 2010) — the proficient-standard column IS the construction
429	definition, reusable verbatim in generator context and reviewer rubric; where a
430	graded verdict is wanted, an analytic rubric with written per-level anchors
431	(Brookhart 2013; Ragas score-anchored form; AAC&U Benchmark→Capstone ladder for
432	draft/ship/exemplary bars, WCAG's cumulative levels as the same device). (c)
433	Completion contracts take DoD form with a consequence rule (2020 Scrum Guide).
434	(d) All derived checklists obey Gawande/Boorman constraints — typed DO-CONFIRM
435	or READ-DO, anchored to named pause points, 5–9 killer items — and their items
436	are added/retired from observed defects (Fagan/Brykczynski). (e) Review rubrics
437	take Google's two-layer form: one senior decision principle ("definitely
438	improves artifact health") + a per-kind aspect list regenerated from the
439	construction definition, with authority routing so linter-owned rules leave the
440	rubric. (f) Guideline documents adopt the Google/Microsoft anatomy — voice
441	principles, condensed highlights (the compiled-into-context layer), topical
442	rules with before/after pairs (Plain Language Guidelines form), word list,
443	explicit precedence hierarchy — with mechanical checks packaged Vale-style:
444	each rule = pattern + severity + link back to its defining guideline. WCAG's
445	normative/informative split governs the whole layer: criteria bind; intent
446	docs and techniques inform (WCAG 2.2).
447	
448	**2.6 Qualitative fitness tests — adapt: Gherkin authoring surface over the
449	established scenario+criteria+judge pattern (see section 3 for the verdict).**
450	Concretely: small sets (3–10 cases) per generated-output kind, each case Given
451	(context) / When (activity) / Then (one falsifiable observable property per
452	clause), compiled 1:1 into an established judge format — promptfoo llm-rubric
453	assertions or G-Eval criteria+evaluation_steps — and executed under Anthropic's
454	grader hierarchy (code checks first, LLM judge only for what code cannot check,
455	human calibration sampled per EvalGen). Judge conventions: one dimension per
456	judgment, constrained verdicts with anchored meanings (autoevals choice_scores;
457	Ragas anchors), reasoning before verdict, judge model and prompt version pinned
458	(Zheng 2023; arXiv:2410.07137). CheckList's capability×test-type matrix is the
459	ideation device when deriving cases from a construction definition.
460	
461	**2.7 Compiled-context and skill governance — adopt Agent Skills + Claude Code
462	memory discipline; adapt the Cursor activation taxonomy, llms.txt index, and
463	Langfuse promotion algebra.**
464	Concretely: one activity per skill in SKILL.md form with the authoring rules
465	and evaluation-first loop (Anthropic best practices; the {skills, query, files,
466	expected_behavior[]} eval structure is the fitness-set container, run via a
467	promptfoo-style colocated config since Anthropic ships no runner); role primers
468	under the 200-line budget with the standing-facts-vs-procedure discriminator
469	and verifiable-specificity rule (Claude Code memory docs); the context-vs-
470	enforcement boundary maps onto definitions-vs-mechanical-checks. Deltas from
471	neighbors: every compiled-context artifact declares its activation mode
472	(always / model-judged / path-conditional / manual — Cursor's taxonomy as
473	vocabulary, not .mdc files); catalog surfaces take llms.txt shape (name,
474	one-line summary, annotated links, explicit Optional tier); canonical-template
475	promotion is a gated act distinct from authoring, and each shop/BC records
476	which definition versions it runs (Langfuse's immutable-version/mutable-label
477	algebra, realized in git + the shopsystem-templates pipeline, not a registry
478	product). AGENTS.md's schema-less model is explicitly rejected for anything
479	checks derive from — nothing mechanical can be derived from a file with no
480	required structure (agents.md). Anthropic's context-engineering principles
481	(smallest high-signal token set; right altitude; named sections; condensed
482	subagent summaries) are adopted as citable principle statements from which
483	these format choices derive.
484	
485	**Bespoke residue.** No container format needs inventing. The bespoke elements
486	are: the shop-native content of the schemas (which outcomes, states, and fields
487	each kind carries), the composed principle-fitness rubric (2.4), and the
488	Gherkin surface for fitness tests (section 3) — each justified above or below.
489	
490	---
491	
492	## 3. The Gherkin-fitness proposal
493	
494	The proposal (product authority, re-founding dialogue; recorded in
495	sessions/sess-2026-08-05-b.md): express qualitative fitness tests for
496	non-deterministic LLM-generated output as Given/When/Then Gherkin scenarios,
497	explicitly not backed by executable step definitions — evaluated by an LLM
498	reviewer — with a small set per output type.
499	
500	**Prior art.** The exact combination — Gherkin syntax judged by an LLM instead
501	of bound to step definitions — has no established named standard; the BDD×LLM
502	literature runs the other direction, LLMs generating or rubric-assessing
503	Gherkin (arXiv:2403.14965; arXiv:2508.20744; arXiv:2607.01980;
504	arXiv:2512.01232). The underlying semantics, however, are firmly established:
505	LangWatch Scenario ships scenario-shaped tests whose assertions are
506	plain-language criteria evaluated by a Judge Agent (github.com/langwatch/
507	scenario); promptfoo's scenarios + llm-rubric YAML is structurally isomorphic
508	(vars = Given/When, rubric assertion = Then; promptfoo.dev); G-Eval canonizes
509	criteria → evaluation steps → judged score (arXiv:2303.16634). The proposal is
510	therefore a thin syntax adaptation of orthodox practice, not a new evaluation
511	paradigm — which is what satisfies the bespoke-requires-justification bar, the
512	justification being literacy reuse: Gherkin is already this shop's
513	behavior-contract vocabulary (features/ tree, scenario hashes,
514	assign_scenarios), and the literature confirms G/W/T is LLM-friendly structure
515	(arXiv:2403.14965).
516	
517	**Strengths.** (1) One authoring literacy across behavior contracts and fitness
518	tests — the PO writes both. (2) G/W/T forces context (Given) and activity
519	(When) to be explicit, which judge prompts need anyway (G-Eval
520	evaluation_params; promptfoo vars). (3) One-clause-one-property aligns with
521	Anthropic's one-isolated-judge-per-dimension rule. (4) "Small set" is the
522	established norm, not a compromise: CheckList MFTs are small targeted probes
523	(arXiv:2005.04118), and EvalGen shows criteria sets grow from observed
524	failures rather than upfront enumeration (arXiv:2404.12272).
525	
526	**Failure modes and mitigations.**
527	- Unfalsifiable Then-clauses ("Then the brief is compelling") — the judge will
528	  pass vibes. Mitigation: an authoring rule that every Then names an observable
529	  property whose violation a reviewer could point at (Deming's test/criterion/
530	  decision discipline), phrased binary or score-anchored (Ragas; autoevals
531	  choice_scores).
532	- Judge gameability and Goodharting — proven by the null-model result
533	  (arXiv:2410.07137) and the bias catalog (arXiv:2306.05685); acute here
534	  because generator and judge are LLMs in one system with retry loops.
535	  Mitigation: keep judge rubrics out of the generator's context where feasible;
536	  delimit the evaluated artifact as untrusted data; different model family or
537	  at least separated context for judging; reasoning-before-verdict; human
538	  spot-audits; never judge-pass-rate as the sole gate for high-stakes
539	  artifacts.
540	- Executable-culture confusion — every established Gherkin ecosystem assumes
541	  step definitions exist (cucumber.io), so judged features will eventually be
542	  fed to a runner or "fixed" by an agent that binds steps. Mitigation: hard
543	  segregation (a distinct tree such as fitness/, never features/; a mandatory
544	  tag such as @judged; a header comment stating evaluation semantics) plus a
545	  schema-level marker in the artifact-kind definition.
546	- Criteria drift — criteria cannot be fully specified a priori
547	  (arXiv:2404.12272). Mitigation: fitness sets are versioned living artifacts
548	  with a standing calibration loop of sampled product-authority grading, not
549	  immutable specs.
550	- Silent judge variance. Mitigation: pin judge model and prompt-template
551	  version alongside the feature file.
552	
553	**Alternatives doing the same job.** Adopt promptfoo YAML directly (established
554	format and runner; loses the Gherkin literacy); LangWatch Scenario criteria
555	lists (established, agent-oriented; heavier multi-turn machinery than artifact
556	fitness needs); plain per-kind rubric documents in G-Eval criteria+steps form
557	(simplest; loses the scenario framing that binds a test to a concrete
558	situation).
559	
560	**Verdict: ADAPT — evidence-based.** The pattern beneath the proposal is
561	orthodox, shipping practice; the Gherkin surface is a justified bespoke twist.
562	It works under these conditions: (a) every Then-clause passes the
563	falsifiability rule; (b) judged features are hard-segregated and marked,
564	schema-level, as non-executable; (c) each Then compiles mechanically 1:1 to a
565	rubric assertion in an established judge format, so the judged semantics rest
566	on established tooling rather than a bespoke runner; (d) judges are
567	bias-hardened and pinned; (e) a human calibration loop with sampled grading
568	exists and feeds revisions. Absent (a)–(c) in particular, the proposal degrades
569	into vibes-with-keywords and should not proceed.
570	
571	---
572	
573	## 4. Open questions for the authority
574	
575	1. Normative-language style: BCP 14 ALL-CAPS keywords or ISO shall/should —
576	   one must be chosen and enforced; both are established, they cannot be mixed
577	   (RFC 8174; ISO/IEC Directives Part 2).
578	2. Decision-record house form: stay pure Nygard (current practice), or move to
579	   MADR v4.0.0 for its Confirmation section and machine-parseable front matter?
580	3. Shop-native state vocabulary: which Essence-style alphas/states name the
581	   shop's trackable concerns (Intent, Scenario Set, Dispatch, Reconciliation…)?
582	   This is product vocabulary the research cannot settle.
583	4. Verdict granularity per artifact kind: binary DoD-style gates, or graded
584	   Benchmark→Capstone / WCAG-level ladders (draft vs ship vs exemplary) — and
585	   for which kinds?
586	5. Compilation target commitment for judged fitness tests: promptfoo as the
587	   established runner, or an in-house minimal judge harness that consumes the
588	   same compiled form? (Tool coupling vs bespoke-runner risk.)
589	6. How much 330xx-style traceability ceremony to carry: explicit
590	   outcome→indicator→rubric tables per process, or by-convention linking only?
591	7. Calibration governance: who grades sampled judge verdicts, at what cadence,
592	   and where is the calibration record kept (per EvalGen the loop is
593	   non-optional; its ownership is a judgment call)?
594	8. Scope of the principle set: target size (order of ten per GOV.UK/TOGAF
595	   guidance) and whether shop principles are one set or split
596	   canonical-vs-shop-local along the existing .claude/canonical vs .claude/shop
597	   line.

## Overview

Clause 7.5 of ISO 9001:2015 focuses on the control of documented information within the quality management system and outlines requirements for creating, updating, controlling, and making available documented information necessary for the effectiveness of the quality management system.

## Creating and Updating (Clause 7.5.2)

Clause 7.5.2 is titled "Creating and updating documented information" and outlines the requirements for the organization to create, review, approve, and update documented information in a controlled manner.

Specifically, organizations are required to ensure when creating and updating documented information that it has suitable identification and description (e.g., title, date, author, reference number), relevant format and media (paper, electronic), and appropriate review and approval for suitability and adequacy.

## Control of Documented Information (Clause 7.5.3)

Requirements include controlling document distribution, ensuring that relevant versions of documents are available at points of use, preventing the unintended use of obsolete documents, and identifying changes and the current revision status of documents.

## Key Context

The 2015 version merged previous requirements for documents and records into a unified approach known as "documented information," with the change in terminology allowing organizations to adopt a broader perspective on how they control and manage information within their quality management systems.

## Key Findings:

**Shewhart's 1939 Framework:**
Shewhart's book "Statistical Methods from the Viewpoint of Quality Control," published in 1939, first introduced the concept of a straight-line, three-step scientific process of specification, production, and inspection. In this framework, specification, production, and inspection correspond to hypothesizing, carrying out an experiment, and testing the hypothesis, respectively.

**Evolution to a Cycle:**
Shewhart eventually clarified that the steps should go in a circle rather than a straight line, and that concept became what is known as the Shewhart Cycle.

**Deming's Modifications:**
Dr. Deming built off of Shewhart's Cycle and modified it. In his new version of the Cycle, debuted in 1950, he stressed the importance of constant interaction among the four steps of design, production, sales, and research. 

**PDSA vs PDCA:**
Deming never liked the word 'check' and preferred 'study' – hence Deming's PDSA cycle, which he always referred to as the 'Shewhart cycle for Learning and Improvement'.

The search results show how Shewhart's foundational work on quality control in 1939 directly led to what became known as the PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle through Deming's later modifications and applications.

## CTQ Tree Overview

A Critical to Quality Tree (also known as a CTQ Tree) is a Six Sigma tool used to identify the needs of the customer and translate that information into measurable product and process requirements.

## Three-Level Derivation Structure

The CTQ tree follows a hierarchical structure with three main components that derive from customer needs to measurable requirements:

1. **Customer Need**: What customer need are you fulfilling with your product or service?

2. **Quality Drivers**: What elements or characteristics will your customers mostly likely consider when judging the quality of your product or service?

3. **Performance Requirements**: What process or product requirements are needed to make those drivers meet customer standards?

## Purpose and Application

Mapping need → driver → requirement clarifies CTQs, sets sigma targets, and focuses resources on features customers value most highly. Six Sigma teams usually start with VoC data when defining a problem and identifying the goals for a project in the Define phase of DMAIC methodology.

## Process Framework

The implementation begins with capturing the Voice of the Customer, identifying critical needs, and breaking these down into specific CTQs. Developing a CTQ Tree visually links broad customer needs to detailed quality requirements, helping stakeholders understand and meet key performance indicators.

## DMAIC Overview

DMAIC is a structured problem-solving approach used to improve existing processes that don't meet performance standards or customer expectations. The approach is used primarily in continuous improvement, lean, and Six Sigma, but also can be implemented as a standalone quality improvement procedure or part of other process improvement initiatives.

## The Five Phases

In Lean Six Sigma, DMAIC is an acronym that represents the five phases of a process improvement methodology: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control.

## Tollgate Reviews

Every phase has defined deliverables and tollgate reviews where sponsors and Master Black Belts verify that the thinking is sound before proceeding. A tollgate review is a formal project checkpoint at the end of each DMAIC phase where the project sponsor, Champion, and Master Black Belt review the team's work, verify that phase deliverables are complete and of sufficient quality, and give formal approval to proceed to the next phase.

## Quality Resources

The search results show that ASQ (American Society for Quality) maintains comprehensive resources on DMAIC at asq.org, including quality tools, certifications, case studies, and detailed phase information. You can find their DMAIC resources directly at asq.org/quality-resources/dmaic.

## Definition

CTQ trees (critical-to-quality trees) are the key measurable characteristics of a product or process whose performance standards or specification limits must be met in order to satisfy the customer. A CTQ Tree is a method to define customer needs into specific, measurable, and actionable performance requirements.

## Connection to Voice of Customer

The CTQ Tree translates customer needs into quantified requirements for the product or service. VOC is understood as understanding customer requirements to find what is important to them, called CTQs, which are measurable customer satisfaction metrics. CTQ characteristics are the measurable attributes essential to meeting customer expectations and are derived from VoC data and specify the performance standards a product or service must achieve to be considered successful by the customer.

## CTQ Tree Structure

CTQs are used to decompose broad customer requirements into more easily quantified elements. Each top-level element (need) is defined in detail by one or more critical quality characteristics (drivers) that affect customer satisfaction, and drivers are translated into measurable product specifications (requirements) that allow companies to deliver the specific quality characteristics customers want.

## Use in Six Sigma

CTQ trees are often used as part of Six Sigma methodology to help prioritize such requirements. In Six Sigma, CTQ metrics bridge the Voice of the Customer and improvement initiatives.

The standard distinguishes between two types of documented information:
